name: Posts
summary: Drafts of what this project will say outside itself, and the text of everything already said. Delivery is your agent's, through a tool you connected to it.
description: Posts holds two things and reaches nothing. A draft is what the project is about to say, written for one named network — the section knows how long a post may be there and who may read one, and counts down while somebody writes. A publication is what it said, carrying the text exactly as it went out, so editing a draft afterwards cannot rewrite the account of it. Both are ordinary records: they live in the project's memory, travel with the repository, and can be written or read by an agent as easily as by a person. Sending is deliberately not here. Sync has no connection to any network and stores no account for one; pressing Publish hands the post to an agent, which delivers it with a tool somebody connected to that agent — an MCP server for that network. So this section is worth installing where an agent has hands, and where one has not, it is a good place to write and a place that will tell you plainly that nothing can go out. Publishing is a person's act either way: there is no clock in here, and nothing that sends anything while nobody is looking.
